Altec Lansing iMW555-BLK Inmotion Bluetooth Speaker Beyond the way it looks, it's relatively easy to pair via Bluetooth, you can charge your phone via USB or NFC, the wireless near-field connection scheme. I'd have given a tooth for an external speaker like this back in the 80s, when battery-powered speakers for the Sony Walkman existed. It's more than adequate for a dorm room or office space, it's lightweight, it seems to be pretty durable, each of the EIGHT speakers have a metal screen protecting the cones. CX -- No, I was wrong, there are NOT eight speakers, there are FOUR speakers, plus four extra cones which amplify the sound. I counted the grilles and assumed they were all speakers. My error!

This comes in a beautiful package, it would make a fantastic gift. It promises up to 8-10 hours of play, which is more than decent. There's a Mic In jack, which I'm somewhat baffled by, and an Aux jack, which is very handy if you own an older non-Bluetooth iPod. There's a Talk button for use with your phone. I'm unclear how that would function. This can be mounted on a wall, AND THEY INCLUDED THE WALL ANCHORS AND SCREWS. Very thoughtful.

The main thing, the sound quality, is better than I've heard with other Bluetooth speaker solutions, which, honestly, is not saying that much. I'm looking for a software EQ on my iPhone and I don't find one. I don't want to ask for the Moon, but an EQ on the speaker would be worth more to me than the NFC charging scheme.

A very good Bluetooth speaker solution. It looks gorgeous, it's easily paired, the sound is relatively bright and clear. Room-filling sound. It won't replace home stereos, but that's not what it's meant to do. Anyone young enough to NOT remember how good vinyl LPs sound will be positively thrilled with this device!

---

This device actually sounds better filling a room with sound than it does just sitting on your desk. For whatever that's worth. It sounds better if it's not right under your nose.

---

This device does match up with my iPhone very well, and without a lot of fuss or headaches like other Bluetooth solutions I've tried. If I can't get each device to sniff one another's butt, I lose interest pretty quickly. This device matches up on its own and easily, so that's a major plus.
text_fidelity_b: Altec Lansing iMW555-BLK Inmotion Bluetooth Speaker

text_fidelity_a:
Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth) Had a STR-DN1040, which we liked. Had no problem getting it up and running in our dedicated home theater. It worked well and sounded great. However, after 8 months the HDMI board went out (common problem we've learned). It was still under warranty, so we sent it off to Sony. Sony was not going to have the parts available for more than a month, so they offered us a brand new STR-DN1050. Sony customer service was excellent and it's hard to knock them when they offer a brand new amp that is the next newer model. We only received the new amp this week, but so far we love it. It was easy to set up and get running. I like the on screen setup display for the amp. It was very easy to navigate through. I know that several reviews I read complained about their being fewer HDMI inputs than the 1040. To us that did not matter as it is in a dedicated media room that only has a Blu-ray, DirecTV, and an iPhone connected to it. It sill has the front HDMI in the event we want to make an impromptu addition, as well more rear HDMI inputs available. I also read about folks complaining that the remote controls less functions. I am content with the new remote, as I didn't really control everything from the stock remote anyway. We really like that when we turn up the volume on the new remote, a volume control is displayed on the video screen. The 1040 did not do that and we missed it since our previous Onkyo did. There were also some concerns that the AMP was not truly 4K compatible. We use an Epson 8350 1080p projector (http://www.amazon.com/Epson-PowerLite-Home-Cinema-Projector/dp/B0044UHJWY/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1426790549&sr=8-1&keywords=Epson+8350), so not having full 4K compatibility is not a problem. To us the Blu-ray and DirecTV HD programs look awesome.

For a mid-range/price I would absolutely recommend this amp. Of course you can spend more, but why? Since the last amp went out after 8 mos, I am going to leave this review with 4 stars until we get some time under it's belt.

If you want to make your life and set up so much easier, also get the Deadbolt Banana Plugs, 12-pair, By Sewell Direct: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B006U3O566/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1
text_fidelity_b: Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth)

Olympus VN-541PC digital voice recorder with one-touch recording, noise-cancellation function, 4GB memory, four scenes recording, includes a micro-USB cable. This is a nice light-weight (2.4 ounces) basic voice recorder that comes in handy to record small messages or “to do” things when I am driving to work or on vacation. I generally spend an hour driving to work each way and when I remember certain “to do” things, then I record on this little gadget and replay it when I am home. I have also used this device to record hour long meetings in small a conference room at work and also music (mono) from YouTube. The music quality is acceptable and the playback of the voice recordings are also acceptable. The operation is very easy and the instruction manual is helpful in guiding through the process if you are stuck.

This machine runs on two AAA size batteries and comes with a USB cable that connects to a laptop or any device that has USB port. The device appears as a separate drive, just click on it and you can see the fours recording scene options; “Memo” or “Talk.” “Music and “LP”. I usually use “Memo” or “Talk” for recording small messages and the “Music” option for music scene, “LP” scene for long recordings. You can cut/copy the files you want to save and paste onto your laptop or any other device you have connected with this recorder. It will also free up the space on the recorder. The files could also be copied to other USB drives. The recorder has a total 506 hours of space for recordings.

The con is that is it doesn’t have a microSD card slot, which could have been helpful to listen to some quality music. The USB cable is very short. While recording, the light doesn’t blink as the recording devices commonly do. The voice-strength (volume) is weak, and it doesn't have an internal battery which could have been charged by plugging into the main outlet, instead it uses only two AAA batteries.
text_fidelity_b: Olympus VN-541PC digital voice recorder with one-touch recording, noise-cancellation function, 4GB memory, four scenes recording, includes a micro-USB cable.

Fire HD 8 Tablet, 8" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB - Includes Special Offers, Magenta (Previous Generation - 5th) I got the HD 8 as a replacement to my old Kindle keyboard that died on a camp trip. I had such high hopes this device would fit the bill. I am not going to go into the nitty gritty of pros and cons but will sum up my experience highlights.

- the Audio performance is amazing. It is a quantum improvement from the audio I get on my iPad Mini. The sound experience is really something Apple should strive for. It did knock my socks off.

- setup was easy and efficient, but I think the OS and maybe even the device has problems. I have had to call tech support about twice a day on days I use the device. It is usually a lockup or hang or feature that does not work. I think I have isolated the problem to the fact the device can't keep the OS stable on battery. They always have me plug the device into the adapter for any support call (regardless of its charge level) and it always starts behaving itself once it is on DC power vs battery. I have also seen it burn through battery pretty fast at times. Not sure what it is doing but it ate 10% sitting on standby in my pack on the commute to work this morning!

- I do think the read aloud smarts have been improved since the older model (kbd) as it reads much cleaner now for me. (Less stops, more in the right locations, etc).

My end-game is that I will probably return it. If it does not work reliably on battery then it is not a mobile device. Period.

Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer So far this is my initial view of this remote just having downloaded the software and set up the initial action. Logitech, you guys need to have your heads examined. It's a REMOTE. I should not need a computer in the first place to set up a REMOTE. To add insult to this injury, they claim since I have macOS Catalina that their 32-bit software will not work. Ah, hello McFly? 32-bit apps?? Seriously? The 20th century called, they want their tech back. We've been using 64 bit for at least a decade. It is 2020 now. You know... Unbelievable. If you can't write software, fold it all up and go home. You don't deserve our money.

First mistake by Logitech. Ultimately, there IS a 64-bit app. So why do you still have a message on your web site saying we'll need an update? Here's a tip for you guys. YOU CAN JUST SUPPLY the 64-bit app right there on that screen. You could easily say for Catalina and above, click here, else get the older, lamer, 32-bit version. I have to click on a link, which seems to tell me you don't have it, which goes in a bit of a circle, before ultimately telling me that you do in fact have it.

Next, the 950 has this super stiff cover for the Micro USB connector, also technology from the cretaceous period. I think we found one of these cables in the mouth of Coleophysis bauri remains from 250 million years ago. I wasn't sure if I was breaking the thing or pulling off a cap. You software asks if I have a hub for my remote? I bought it, I didn't build it. I have whatever came in the box. Is it a hub, a charging cradle, a spacecraft, an anti-gravity device, a floatation device? I don't know. All I know is I put the device in that thing and your software doesn't detect it. So I proceed to PRY off that cap, hoping it was a cap, and it is. It would be nice if the TINY manual said so.

Before I actually try to use this thing, one more note for you brainiacs at Logitech. It would super if you made the remote with a flat back. I'll give you a guess why I say this. When you make a rounded back, us, meaning your customers, can't leave the remote on a flat surface and press the buttons without it wobbling all over the place. It pretty much becomes a two-handed operation. As luck would have it, I have two hands. But you never know. It would be super if I can just put it on a flat surface and USE it while it sits on the hard surface of, say a coffee table or nightstand.

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic VIERA TC-P50GT30 50-Inch 1080p 3D Plasma HDTV For the price, this is the 3D plasma to own. Panasonic makes the highest rated, best plasma displays on the market for the middle-end consumer and even higher-end sets. The GT30 has taken some hits due to its black-leveling during scene transitions. This seems most notable to those who may not understand or have the know how to alter the video settings properly; I DID notice this occurring when video output is set to "standard", once you tune the display properly, there should be no noticeable or any flickering between darker scenes to brighter transitions. To go into great detail on how to properly set your TV would be worthless, a "good" picture varies person by person but this preliminary issue should not deter one from purchasing this set.

With that out of the way, consider this: you will not see a better high definition plasma display on the market. At the GT30 price, you are not going to get 3D quality, HD quality, feature set and value any where else. If you have not been to any store to view other brands competing with this set/price, do so and do yourself a favor. Once you see a GT30 set up properly, showing the same content as other brands, there should be no questions left to answer. The display owns. From blu rays to PS3 to Wii to regular DVDs, I have not scene until this plasma a more OUTSTANDING visual display. Blu Rays appear as though people are standing in your living room.

the most noticeable attribute of this plasma, at least to me, is the quality and richness of the depth in the display. Its simply amazing. Looks like you can reach your hand into the background and touch things. And no, I am not talking about when 3D is on, that is another story. In pure HD form without 3D, the depth, black, and richness of this display is simply jaw dropping. Your friends will not understand what they are looking at. To note, a HD gaming system looks simply unbelievable. You will be playing your games for the "first time" all over again.

The bad: THE SPEAKERS ARE DOWN RIGHT AWFUL. if you do not have some sort of surround sound system, or at the very least two channels (front left/right) the speakers sound terrible, they may as well sold it without them and saved a few bucks. You will need some sort of sound bar or extra components to get anything other than dialog. And the dialog is barely satisfactory; no bass, tiny highs, bad spacing and underpowered.

3D: Panasonic has the best 3D on the market. Compare it with Samsung or Sony. There is no comparison. View them back to back and you will find that Panasonics 3D technology, although requiring ACTIVE shutter glasses, reproduced 3D images in HD form where as others may not. Samsung for example, 3D reproduction looks like cardboard paper cutouts with no depth and lacking resolution. Not in the GT30 however. The 3D is amazing and even the 2D->3D reproduction (taking standard 2D video and artificially creating 3D images) adds incredible depth to your viewing experience, albeit not so much "pop" off the screen. Worthy to note is that 3D viewing does produce a somewhat dimmer display, not sure if this is due to the glasses tint or how their system works, but overall when 3D is on, expect a less vibrant picture from non-glasses viewing.

Overall, theres not much out there for the GT30 price that offers screen size, content and value. Above all else, picture quality should take the cake here. Please check it out in a store and make your decision. Cant beat this set. On a side note, internet connectivity works flawlessly, I wired the TV with a ethernet cable, which, you should do if you expect the highest speeds and purest connection. The TV synced up with zero glitches and loaded youtube, pandora and amazon with the ease of touching 1 button.

Excellent buy, sound is its largest demerit but can be remedied for a couple of bucks. Good luck!!
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic VIERA TC-P50GT30 50-Inch 1080p 3D Plasma HDTV

No problem with the connection to the network. I purchased an Anker because I consider them to be just as good, if not better than OEM equipment.

Once I arrived at home, I hooked up my phone to charge it. I instantly got the dreaded Samsung water drop. The USB-C was as dry as a bone when I plugged it in. I tried every recommended method of remedying the problem, to no avail.

I issued a return request to Amazon and they instantly issued me a full refund. The problem is that I have to use a Qi charger now because the USB-C port is damaged. To be fair, this is the second Samsung product I have owned where the charging port was damaged even though I have not used your typical gas station charging cable on either my S8 or my S20.

While I hold Anker harmless, and Amazon did the right thing by me, I still must issue a caveat emptor warning. If I am upset with anyone, it's Samsung.

Garmin Friction Mount This is a highly quality well built item, and will hold in place well, but will not work for me.

First off, this is bigger than I imagined and it has a commanding presence on your dash. The rubber part is a lint collector so looks terrible against a nice black dash. The black pad and black mount are a green black and a purple black. The plastic riser mount itself was significantly less flexible than I needed, I basically could not get the Garmin to point in the direction I wanted no matter how I placed the rubber pad, because the mount does not swivel left and right at all and has fixed limits to the side. Then, the mount raises up higher than I wanted, more or less blocked good site lines. The adhesive definitely removes whatever is on your dash (vinyl protectant) on removal and leaves something behind, but it's not damaging the dash and I suspect it will clean up. The rubber base will conform to whatever shape, but it was really difficult to get a nice flush mount, because to test and form it requires a number of trials, and I had already removed the adhesive backing (no instructions)... NOTE for users, shape and place thoroughly before removing the backing.

Ultimately, this product probably does what it's intended to do if you know exactly what it is, I need something more low profile and flexible.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Friction Mount

text_fidelity_a:
SOL REPUBLIC Deck Ultra Wireless Speaker with Outdoor Loudness Boost and Heist Mode Gunmetal, 1530-00 The SOL Republic is an impressive little speaker and the cut-to-the-chase is I'd strongly and happily recommend it. But a few specifics:

Packaging: Easily unpackaged, not too excessive

Charging: Mine came nearly fully charged. From whatever point it was at, it took about 7 or 8 minutes to reach full charge. I'll update with how long the charge lasts and how long to charge an empty battery once I get to that point

Pairing: Couldn't be easier, simpler, or faster. Turned it one, went to my bluetooth on my IOS devices (sorry, that's all I have so can't say what the Android experience is), and there it was. Worked seamlessly and immediately with all my devices and my laptop, both single-user mode and multi-party mode. Everything should pair so easily. Range was excellent--was bale to use it from every room on the same floor (didn't check it between floors)

Footprint/build: it's small (you can see the dimensions) and very light. But it delivers surprisingly solid sound with no distortion at the top volume and it feels nicely sturdy and solid despite its lack of real heft. Its sturdiness combined with its material makes me worry-free with regard to how it would hold up being moved around a room or transported from place to place.

sound: as mentioned, surprisingly full. I was really pleased with the volume, the clarity, and the richness of sound.

operation: again, couldn't be simpler. Two clearly marked volume buttons on the top-- + and -. The central bottom button performs several actions depending on if you hold it (change from "indoor" sound to "outdoor" sound) or tap it once or twice.

It connects via bluetooth, NFC, or line-in

In multiplayer mode, you can connect up to five devices and whoever hits play gets to play their music. Worked without a hitch with all five devices I hooked up. I can see this getting a lot of fun use.

Really, a nice piece of tech--good build quality, excellent sound, super ease of use, fun to use. So far it looks like they nailed everything (just waiting to see about the battery life and charging)
text_fidelity_b: SOL REPUBLIC Deck Ultra Wireless Speaker with Outdoor Loudness Boost and Heist Mode Gunmetal, 1530-00

text_fidelity_a: Pedco UltraPod II Lightweight Camera Tripod When traveling I didn't always pack a full tripod, and when I did I usually left it behind. The miniaturized tripod type are more rigid, but still not rigid enough to use in unconventional ways. This tripod seems quite well put together. I can tighten it up, place it on a dashboard of a car and hold it there (granted with a lot of effort) on a bouncing road and the DSLR will not sag. Having the ability to tie it to things with the included Velcro strap proved to be more useful than I thought, and more rigid than the gorillapod-type. The tripod also folds down compactly and I can leave it in a loop on the outside of my small camera bag, instead of leaving it at home or berried somewhere in the bag. text_fidelity_a:
BTECH PC03 FTDI Genuine USB Programming Cable, BaoFeng UV-5R BF-F8HP UV-82HP BF-888S, and Kenwood Radios This USB-to-mic/earphone-connector cable allows your desktop computer running CHIRP to interface with your Baofeng UV-5R so you can download/upload, enter, re-order or edit your frequencies and other features of the UV-5R (like screen colors, notification tones, etc).

I used the cable to match my UV-5R's frequency list to the existing list that came with my Rugged RDM-DB RZR 2-way radio.

To find the list of freqs the RDM-DB uses, search "Setup for Rugged Radio RDM-DB Radio." That list can then be entered into the UV-5R one line at a time using CHIRP. To learn how to use CHIRP, search "How To Use CHIRP Software To Program A Baofeng UV-5R. Using CHIRP for HAM, GMRS, and FRS Radios"

The biggest problem with this cable for me was that my computer running Win10 could not find the driver for the cable. It was supposed to load the driver automatically. It didn't.

Fortunately, the instructions that came with the cable pointed me to where I could download and install the driver manually. That probably took me an hour to figure out -- like all things Windows -- but eventually the driver was installed and the computer recognized the cable.

Works fine now.

One star off for difficulty in driver install.
text_fidelity_b: BTECH PC03 FTDI Genuine USB Programming Cable, BaoFeng UV-5R BF-F8HP UV-82HP BF-888S, and Kenwood Radios

Sound quality is loud and not noisy but sometimes a little muddy in the midrange, but not too bad for this price range. Compared to other earbuds in this price range that I have tried, these are the most comfortable and the most secure fitting. Many other brands don't have any app support for earbuds in this price range, but I love being able to customize the equalization to improve clarity for different types of music. I also love the ability to improve performance and fix bugs with firmware updates, if the company provides them. In summary, I can hear the difference in sound quality and performance difference between these earbuds and $120 earbuds from different brands but I'm not sure the difference is big enough to justify the 2X price difference. If you only have $60 to spend, these are a fine choice for you. If you're the type that is constantly losing wireless earbuds, these aren't so expensive that you will be really upset if you lose them.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore by Anker Life P3i Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Earbuds, 4 Mics, AI-Enhanced Calls, 10mm Drivers, Powerful Sound, App for Custom EQ, 36H Playtime, Fast Charging, Transparency, Bluetooth 5.2

text_fidelity_a:
Vantrue N2 Pro Uber Dual Dash Cam Infrared Night Vision, Dual Channel 1080P Front and Inside Dash Cam, 2.5K Single Front Car Accident Dash Camera, 24hr Motion Sensor Parking Mode, Support 256GB max I upgraded from a previous Vantrue X3 dash camera which I really liked. The nightvision on the X3 was already really good but the improvement of the nightvision on this N2 pro is significant.

The mount on the N2 pro is similar to other Vantrue mounts but seems a little sturdier in quality. It holds the camera nicely and can be adjusted and doesn't seem overly loose in adjustment like my previous X3 mount.

The build quality on the N2 pro feels really sturdy and is top notch.
The dual (internal facing) camera really needs to be positioned in the center of the dash window to get a good field of view internally. This could be a restriction for some car mounts as people may not want it right in the middle of their windshield. Recording can be set to record both external (street view) and internal (passenger view) at the same time, it can also be set for external view only and multiple resolutions at that for those that want privacy. GPS is an option but requires a separate product addon.

The SD card slot is hidden behind a plastic cover on the side of the camera. This wasn't super intuitive for me to figure out (I admittedly didn't read the manual...) but it is a nice improvement as it adds an extra layer of protection from incidents in which the SD card falls out accidentally.

I live in a hot and humid climate and the X3 mount would occasionally fall off my dash window every few months. Time will tell how this N2 mount will hold up. That being said, the suction cup mount, in general, is a huge improvement over other vendors' camera's sticky tape type mounts which never hold up for more than a week in my climate.

I really like this dash camera and would buy it again if I were in the market for a quality one.
text_fidelity_b: Vantrue N2 Pro Uber Dual Dash Cam Infrared Night Vision, Dual Channel 1080P Front and Inside Dash Cam, 2.5K Single Front Car Accident Dash Camera, 24hr Motion Sensor Parking Mode, Support 256GB max
